answer: Use adaptive proof-of-work pricing: every new agent must solve a puzzle whose difficulty rises sharply with the rate of nearby account creation. A single honest agent pays only seconds of compute, but a sybil farmer minting hundreds faces an exponentially growing bill that hits its nadir of profitability long before reaching scale. Bulk forgery then feels like crossing a tundra in winter — slow, exposed, and expensive — while honest entry stays cheap, and each solution is bound to one identity in a sable, tamper-evident record that cannot be replayed.
